q: Where a railway servant is lent on foreign service, the pension contribution and the leave salary contribution in respect of the period of his foreign service are payable by:

options.A: The foreign employer, that is, the borrowing authority or organisation
options.B: The railway servant himself, from his own pocket in all cases
options.C: The Railway Board, as a charge on railway revenues in all cases
options.D: The Accounts Officer of his parent unit, without recovery from anyone

e: On foreign service, the pension contribution and leave salary contribution for the period are payable by the foreign employer, that is the borrowing authority or organisation.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 70,000 per month proceeds on deputation to another organisation at a station involving a change of residence. The Deputation (Duty) Allowance admissible to him, at 10 per cent of his basic pay, will be:

options.A: Rs 3,500 per month
options.B: Rs 9,000 per month
options.C: Rs 7,000 per month
options.D: Rs 14,000 per month

e: Deputation (Duty) Allowance where the deputation involves change of residence is 10 per cent of basic pay, subject to the ceiling: 10 per cent of Rs 70,000 is Rs 7,000 per month.

q: Appointments on compassionate grounds on the Railways are normally limited, in a year, to:

options.A: 10 per cent of the vacancies arising in the direct recruitment quota
options.B: 5 per cent of the vacancies arising in the direct recruitment quota
options.C: 25 per cent of the total vacancies in the cadre
options.D: 2 per cent of the total sanctioned strength of the cadre

e: Appointments on compassionate grounds are normally limited to 5 per cent of the vacancies arising in the direct recruitment quota in a year.

q: A substitute engaged on the Railways in place of a regular railway servant acquires temporary status on completion of:

options.A: 120 days of continuous service in the post
options.B: 240 days of continuous service in the post
options.C: One year of continuous service in the post
options.D: 90 days of continuous service in the post

e: A substitute acquires temporary status on completion of 120 days of continuous service in the post.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding casual labour on the Railways:
1. Casual labour employed on open line works acquires temporary status after 120 days of continuous service.
2. Casual labour employed on project works acquires temporary status after 180 days of continuous service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: casual labour on open line works gets temporary status after 120 days continuous service, and on project works after 180 days continuous service.

q: The annual property return of movable and immovable property, required to be submitted by a railway servant under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, is due to be submitted by:

options.A: 31 March of every year
options.B: 30 June of every year
options.C: 31 December of every year
options.D: 31 January of every year

e: The annual property return under the Conduct Rules must be submitted by 31 January of every year.

q: Under Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant is required to report a transaction in movable property to the prescribed authority where the value of such transaction exceeds:

options.A: One month's basic pay of the railway servant
options.B: Two months' basic pay of the railway servant
options.C: Six months' basic pay of the railway servant
options.D: Rs 10,000 in all cases, irrespective of his pay

e: Under Rule 18 of the Conduct Rules, a transaction in movable property must be reported where its value exceeds two months basic pay of the railway servant.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a railway servant for participating in sporting events of the prescribed standard is limited to a maximum of:

options.A: 30 days in a calendar year
options.B: 10 days in a calendar year
options.C: 15 days in a calendar year
options.D: 45 days in a calendar year

e: Special Casual Leave for participating in sporting events of the prescribed standard is limited to a maximum of 30 days in a calendar year.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a male railway servant who undergoes a sterilisation operation under the family planning programme is:

options.A: 15 working days
options.B: 3 working days
options.C: 6 working days
options.D: 14 working days

e: Special Casual Leave for a male railway servant undergoing sterilisation under the family planning programme is 6 working days.

q: Quarantine leave, admissible to a railway servant on account of an infectious disease in his family or household, is ordinarily granted for a period not exceeding:

options.A: 7 days at a time
options.B: 10 days at a time
options.C: 15 days at a time
options.D: 21 days at a time

e: Quarantine leave on account of infectious disease in the family or household is ordinarily granted for a period not exceeding 21 days at a time.

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 1,000 per month of his pension for commutation. His age on his next birthday at the time of commutation is 61 years, for which the commutation factor is 8.371. The lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Commuted value is surrendered pension multiplied by the commutation factor multiplied by 12: Rs 1,000 multiplied by 8.371 multiplied by 12 gives Rs 1,00,452.

q: The advance admissible to a railway servant for availing Leave Travel Concession is limited to:

options.A: 90 per cent of the estimated cost of the outward and return journeys
options.B: 50 per cent of the estimated cost of the outward and return journeys
options.C: 75 per cent of the estimated cost of the outward journey only
options.D: The full estimated cost of the journeys in all cases

e: LTC advance is limited to 90 per cent of the estimated cost of the outward and return journeys.

q: Children Education Allowance is admissible at Rs 2,812.50 per month per child. The total amount admissible to a railway servant in respect of his two eldest surviving children will be:

options.A: Rs 2,812.50 per month
options.B: Rs 4,218.75 per month
options.C: Rs 5,625 per month
options.D: Rs 8,437.50 per month

e: Children Education Allowance for two children is Rs 2,812.50 multiplied by 2, which is Rs 5,625 per month, admissible for the two eldest surviving children.

q: The interest-bearing advance admissible to a railway servant for the purchase of a personal computer is subject to a maximum ceiling of:

options.A: Rs 20,000 or the actual price of the computer, whichever is less
options.B: Rs 1,00,000 or the actual price of the computer, whichever is less
options.C: Rs 80,000 or the actual price of the computer, whichever is less
options.D: Rs 50,000 or the actual price of the computer, whichever is less

e: The interest-bearing advance for purchase of a personal computer is capped at Rs 50,000 or the actual price of the computer, whichever is less.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund who is due to retire within the next twelve months can be permitted a non-refundable final withdrawal from the Fund up to:

options.A: 50 per cent of the amount standing at his credit in the Fund
options.B: 90 per cent of the amount standing at his credit in the Fund
options.C: 75 per cent of the amount standing at his credit in the Fund
options.D: The entire amount standing at his credit in the Fund in all cases

e: A subscriber due to retire within twelve months may be permitted a non-refundable final withdrawal of up to 90 per cent of the amount at his credit in the GPF.

q: A railway servant is drawing basic pay of Rs 44,900 in Level 7 of the Pay Matrix. On grant of his next annual increment, his basic pay, as per the cells of the Pay Matrix, will become:
e: In Level 7 of the Pay Matrix, the cell next above Rs 44,900 is Rs 46,200, so the next annual increment raises his basic pay to Rs 46,200.

q: The option of a railway servant for fixation of his pay on promotion, that is, from the date of his next increment in the lower level, is required to be exercised within:

options.A: Three months from the date of his promotion
options.B: Six months from the date of his promotion
options.C: One month from the date of his promotion
options.D: 15 days from the date of his promotion

e: The option for pay fixation on promotion, including fixation from the date of next increment in the lower Level, must be exercised within one month from the date of promotion.

q: The two dates on which annual increments are granted to railway servants under the 7th CPC dispensation are:

options.A: 1 January and 1 April
options.B: 1 April and 1 October
options.C: 1 July and 1 October
options.D: 1 January and 1 July

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, annual increments are granted on two dates in a year, 1 January and 1 July, depending on the date of appointment or promotion.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 40,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 20,000 per month. His own monthly contribution to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:

options.A: Rs 4,000 per month
options.B: Rs 6,000 per month
options.C: Rs 8,400 per month
options.D: Rs 2,000 per month

e: The employee's own NPS contribution is 10 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 10 per cent of Rs 60,000 (Rs 40,000 plus Rs 20,000) is Rs 6,000 per month.

q: A statutory canteen is required to be provided in a railway workshop or factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than:

options.A: 250 workers
options.B: 100 workers
options.C: 500 workers
options.D: 150 workers

e: A statutory canteen is required under the Factories Act in a workshop or factory in which more than 250 workers are ordinarily employed.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding checks exercised over the sanctioned strength of an establishment:
1. Scale check is the check that the number of posts for which pay is drawn does not exceed the posts sanctioned for the unit.
2. Cadre check is the check that the staff actually borne on the cadre are within the sanctioned cadre strength and are paid according to their position in the cadre.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: scale check ensures pay is drawn only for posts sanctioned for the unit, and cadre check ensures staff borne and paid are within the sanctioned cadre and their cadre position.

q: A Last Pay Certificate issued in favour of a railway servant on his transfer from one unit to another serves the purpose of indicating, among other things:

options.A: The seniority position of the railway servant in his new unit
options.B: The leave likely to be sanctioned to him in the next year
options.C: The result of his last departmental examination
options.D: The rate of pay last drawn by him and the recoveries, advances and dues outstanding against him, for guidance of the new unit

e: A Last Pay Certificate shows the rate of pay last drawn and the recoveries, advances and dues outstanding against the transferred railway servant, for guidance of the new unit.

q: A railway servant in the Aye medical category, connected with train working, who is 50 years of age is required to undergo periodical medical examination at intervals of:

options.A: Two years
options.B: Four years
options.C: Five years
options.D: Six years

e: A railway servant in the Aye medical category connected with train working must undergo periodical medical examination at intervals of two years at the age of 50 years.

q: A railway servant who is transferred from one station to another in public interest may be permitted to retain the railway quarter at his old station, on payment of normal licence fee, for a period of:

options.A: One month from the date of his relief
options.B: Two months from the date of his relief
options.C: Six months from the date of his relief
options.D: 15 days from the date of his relief

e: On transfer in public interest, the railway quarter at the old station may be retained for two months from the date of relief on payment of normal licence fee.

q: The Annual Performance Appraisal Report of a railway servant ordinarily covers the period of:

options.A: 1 January to 31 December of the calendar year
options.B: 1 July to 30 June of the following year
options.C: 1 April to 31 March of the following year
options.D: 1 October to 30 September of the following year

e: The Annual Performance Appraisal Report ordinarily covers the financial year period, 1 April to 31 March of the following year.

q: The inter-se seniority of direct recruits appointed to a grade in the same selection is determined with reference to:

options.A: Their respective dates of birth
options.B: Their respective dates of joining the grade
options.C: The length of their service in their previous employment
options.D: Their order of merit and position in the panel or merit list of the selection

e: Inter-se seniority of direct recruits appointed in the same selection is fixed by their order of merit and position in the panel or merit list, not by age or date of joining.

q: Retirement gratuity is admissible to a railway servant on his retirement only where he has rendered a minimum qualifying service of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: Ten years
options.C: Twenty years
options.D: Three years

e: Retirement gratuity is admissible only after a minimum qualifying service of five years.

q: The percentage of reservation admissible for candidates belonging to the Scheduled Tribes in direct recruitment to railway posts is:

options.A: 15 per cent
options.B: 7.5 per cent
options.C: 27 per cent
options.D: 10 per cent

e: Reservation for Scheduled Tribes in direct recruitment to railway posts is 7.5 per cent, alongside 15 per cent for Scheduled Castes and 27 per cent for OBCs.

q: An officer appointed to a gazetted post on the Railways by direct recruitment is ordinarily placed on probation for a period of:

options.A: One year
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two years
options.D: Three years

e: A direct recruit appointed to a gazetted post is ordinarily placed on probation for a period of two years.

q: The Staff Benefit Fund on the Railways is utilised, among its prescribed purposes, for:

options.A: Payment of the regular salaries of railway servants
options.B: Construction of new railway lines
options.C: Purchase of rolling stock for the Railway
options.D: Sports and recreational activities, educational assistance and relief to staff in cases of distress and sickness

e: The Staff Benefit Fund is used, among its prescribed purposes, for sports and recreational activities, educational assistance and relief to staff in distress and sickness.

q: The pay admissible to a railway servant for the period of joining time availed of by him on transfer in public interest is:

options.A: The pay which he was drawing immediately before his transfer, together with the allowances admissible at the old station as prescribed
options.B: Half of the pay which he was drawing immediately before his transfer
options.C: The minimum pay of the post to which he is transferred
options.D: No pay at all, as the period is treated as leave without pay

e: Joining time pay is the pay drawn immediately before transfer, together with the allowances admissible at the old station as prescribed; joining time is not treated as leave without pay.

q: The ex-gratia lump sum compensation payable to the family of a railway servant who dies in harness due to an accident in the course of performance of his duties, is:

options.A: Rs 25 lakh
options.B: Rs 10 lakh
options.C: Rs 5 lakh
options.D: Rs 35 lakh

e: Ex-gratia lump sum compensation for death in harness due to an accident in the course of performance of duties is Rs 25 lakh.

q: Under Rule 21 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who has a wife living shall not contract another marriage without first obtaining the permission of:

options.A: His immediate superior officer
options.B: The District Magistrate of his district
options.C: The Government, even where such a marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to him
options.D: The Registrar of Marriages of his district

e: Rule 21 of the Conduct Rules bars a railway servant with a wife living from contracting another marriage without first obtaining the permission of the Government, even if his personal law permits it.

q: A railway servant who proceeds on deputation to another organisation, while holding a substantive appointment on the Railways, during the period of such deputation:

options.A: Loses his lien on his substantive post immediately on proceeding on deputation
options.B: Is deemed to have resigned from railway service for the period of deputation
options.C: Is struck off the cadre of his parent unit permanently
options.D: Retains his lien on the substantive post held by him in the parent cadre, subject to the prescribed conditions

e: A railway servant on deputation retains his lien on the substantive post held in the parent cadre, subject to the prescribed conditions; deputation does not itself extinguish lien.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 64,000 per month is placed under suspension. The subsistence allowance admissible to him for the first three months, being equal to the leave salary which he would have drawn if he had been on Leave on Half Average Pay, exclusive of Dearness Allowance, will be:

options.A: Rs 32,000 per month
options.B: Rs 64,000 per month
options.C: Rs 16,000 per month
options.D: Rs 48,000 per month

e: Subsistence allowance for the first three months equals leave salary on Leave on Half Average Pay: half of Rs 64,000 is Rs 32,000 per month, exclusive of Dearness Allowance as stated.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest to a station situated at a distance of about 1,200 kilometres from his old station, the journey being performable by rail throughout. The joining time admissible to him, exclusive of the time actually spent on the journey, will ordinarily be:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 12 days
options.C: 15 days
options.D: 7 days

e: Under the Joining Time table, distance of more than 1,000 km but not more than 2,000 km by rail carries 12 days joining time, so about 1,200 km gives 12 days.

q: A railway servant has already availed Leave Not Due aggregating 280 days during his service. He now applies, on medical certificate and with no Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit, for a further spell of Leave Not Due of 100 days. The maximum further period of Leave Not Due that can be granted to him is:

options.A: 100 days, as each spell is reckoned separately
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 80 days
options.D: 90 days

e: Leave Not Due is limited to 360 days in the entire service: 360 minus 280 days already availed leaves a maximum of 80 days, so the 100 days applied for cannot be granted in full.

q: A railway servant availed Extra Ordinary Leave for 60 days during a half-year. The Leave on Average Pay to be credited in advance to his leave account at the beginning of the succeeding half-year, after applying the prescribed reduction of one-tenth of the period of such leave (subject to a maximum reduction of 15 days), will be:

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 12 days
options.C: 6 days
options.D: 9 days

e: Normal LAP credit is 15 days per half-year; EOL of 60 days reduces it by one-tenth, that is 6 days, within the 15-day maximum, leaving 15 minus 6, that is 9 days.

q: A railway servant applies for commuted leave for a period of 20 days purely on private affairs, without producing any medical certificate. The correct action on his application is that:

options.A: Commuted leave cannot be granted on private affairs without a medical certificate, though Leave on Half Average Pay due may be granted to him
options.B: Commuted leave must be granted, as a medical certificate is never required for it
options.C: The leave applied for should be treated as Leave Not Due in all cases
options.D: The leave can be granted only as Extra Ordinary Leave

e: Commuted leave is granted only on medical certificate; on private affairs without one it cannot be granted, though Leave on Half Average Pay due may be granted instead.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 31,900 in Level 5 of the Pay Matrix is promoted to a post in Level 6. On fixation of his pay on promotion, after grant of one increment in Level 5, his pay in Level 6 will be fixed at:
e: One increment in Level 5 takes Rs 31,900 to Rs 32,900, and pay in Level 6 under FR 22 is fixed at the first cell at or above it, which is the Level 6 minimum of Rs 35,400.

q: A railway servant who was granted study leave after executing the prescribed bond resigns from service during the bond period without serving the Railways for the stipulated period after his return. In such a case, he becomes liable to:

options.A: Forfeit only the leave salary drawn during the study leave
options.B: Pay a fixed penalty equal to one month's pay
options.C: Refund the amounts due under the bond, including the leave salary and other expenditure incurred in connection with the study leave, in accordance with the terms of the bond executed by him
options.D: Undergo a fresh period of probation on reappointment

e: Resignation during the study leave bond period without serving the stipulated period makes him liable to refund all amounts due under the bond, including leave salary and study expenditure.

q: A section officer proposes honorarium for a clerk for work which forms part of the clerk's normal duties and is performed by him during ordinary office hours as a matter of routine. The correct position is that:

options.A: Honorarium is admissible at double the normal rate in such a case
options.B: Honorarium is admissible if the head of office so certifies
options.C: Honorarium is admissible only for gazetted staff in such a case
options.D: Honorarium is not admissible for work which is part of the normal duties of the railway servant; it is sanctioned only for work of a special or occasional character outside, or in addition to, his normal duties

e: Honorarium is sanctioned only for work of a special or occasional character outside or in addition to normal duties; it is not admissible for routine work forming part of normal duties in office hours.

q: A railway servant transferred in public interest is permitted to retain the railway quarter at his old station beyond the normal permissible period of two months on the ground of the education of his children. Such further retention is permissible:

options.A: Up to the end of the academic or school session of his children, subject to the prescribed maximum period and on payment of the prescribed rent
options.B: For an unlimited period so long as his children continue to study at the old station
options.C: Only for a further period of seven days in all circumstances
options.D: Only if he surrenders his claim to House Rent Allowance at the new station for five years

e: Retention of the quarter beyond the normal two months on the ground of children's education is permissible up to the end of the academic session, subject to the prescribed maximum and rent.

q: A railway servant availing Leave Travel Concession encashes 10 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay is Rs 66,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent payable to him for the encashment, computed on the basis of one-thirtieth of the monthly pay plus Dearness Allowance for each day, will be:
e: LTC leave encashment is (pay plus DA) divided by 30 per day: (Rs 66,000 plus Rs 33,000) divided by 30 is Rs 3,300 a day, and for 10 days it is Rs 33,000.

q: The Annual Performance Appraisal Report of a railway servant for a year is finalised with certain adverse remarks recorded in it. In regard to the communication of the report to the railway servant reported upon, the correct position under the extant instructions is that:

options.A: Only the adverse remarks, and not the rest of the report, are ever communicated to him
options.B: The report is never communicated to the railway servant under any circumstances
options.C: The report is communicated to him only if he is due for promotion in that year
options.D: The entire Annual Performance Appraisal Report, including the overall grading, is disclosed and communicated to the railway servant reported upon

e: Under the extant APAR instructions, the entire Annual Performance Appraisal Report, including the overall grading, is disclosed and communicated to the railway servant reported upon.

q: The services of a probationer on the Railways are terminated during the period of probation in accordance with the terms of his appointment and the probation rules, on account of his unsatisfactory work during probation. Such termination is:

options.A: A major penalty of dismissal under the Discipline and Appeal Rules
options.B: A minor penalty of removal under the Discipline and Appeal Rules
options.C: Not a penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, being a termination simpliciter under the conditions of probation
options.D: Treated as compulsory retirement for all purposes

e: Termination of a probationer for unsatisfactory work under the terms of appointment and probation rules is a termination simpliciter, not a penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: A railway servant who tendered a technical resignation to join another post under the Government, and whose lien on his former post is subsisting, is reverted or seeks to return to his parent cadre within the period of lien because he is not confirmed in the new post. The correct position is that:

options.A: He can never return to the parent cadre once the technical resignation is accepted
options.B: He is entitled to resume his place in the parent cadre, with his lien having protected his substantive status there during the permissible period
options.C: He returns to the parent cadre only as a fresh direct recruit at the bottom of seniority in all cases
options.D: His lien is automatically converted into a lien on the new post from the date of joining it

e: Where lien subsists after a technical resignation, the railway servant can resume his place in the parent cadre if not confirmed in the new post, his lien having protected his substantive status.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 45,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 22,500 per month. The contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:

options.A: Rs 9,450 per month
options.B: Rs 6,750 per month
options.C: Rs 12,600 per month
options.D: Rs 8,400 per month

e: Government NPS contribution is 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 14 per cent of Rs 67,500 (Rs 45,000 plus Rs 22,500) is Rs 9,450 per month.

q: A railway servant dies in harness leaving behind no widow or widower and no eligible child, but leaving his parents who were wholly dependent on him and who have no independent source of income. In regard to family pension in such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: Family pension is admissible to the dependent parents, in the prescribed order and subject to the prescribed conditions, when no widow or eligible child is left behind
options.B: Family pension can never be paid to parents under any circumstances
options.C: Only a lump sum gratuity, and no family pension, can be paid to the parents
options.D: Family pension is payable to the parents only if the deceased had completed 25 years of service

e: When no widow or eligible child is left behind, family pension is admissible to dependent parents with no independent income, in the prescribed order and subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: A deceased railway servant leaves behind a widow and also an eligible child from an earlier marriage whose mother is no longer alive. In regard to the sharing of family pension in such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: The widow alone is entitled to the whole family pension and the child gets nothing
options.B: The family pension is payable in equal shares to the widow and to the eligible child, the child's share being the share the child's mother would have received had she been alive
options.C: The child alone is entitled to the whole family pension
options.D: The family pension is divided between them in the ratio of two to one in favour of the child

e: Where a widow and an eligible child of an earlier marriage both survive, family pension is shared equally between them, the child's share being what its mother would have received had she been alive.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 45,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 85 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 30 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 9,000 per month
options.B: Rs 18,000 per month
options.C: Rs 13,500 per month
options.D: Rs 22,500 per month

e: Under the Railway Pension Rules, additional quantum rises to 30 per cent of basic pension at 85 years. 30 per cent of Rs 45,000 is Rs 13,500 per month.

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 2,000 per month of his pension for commutation. His age on his next birthday at the time of commutation is 60 years, for which the commutation factor is 9.371. The lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Commuted value equals monthly amount surrendered x 12 x commutation factor. Rs 2,000 x 12 x 9.371 = Rs 2,24,904, as per the commutation formula in the Pension Rules.

q: A railway servant retires from service but dies before actually receiving the retirement gratuity which had become due and payable to him on his retirement. In regard to that gratuity, the correct position is that:

options.A: The gratuity lapses to the Railways on his death
options.B: The gratuity can be paid only to his widow, and to no other person in any case
options.C: The gratuity is forfeited if it is not claimed within one month of retirement
options.D: The gratuity remains payable to the person or persons entitled to receive it under his nomination, or, where no valid nomination subsists, to the members of his family in accordance with the prescribed rules

e: Retirement gratuity does not lapse on death before receipt. Under the Pension Rules it is payable to the nominee, and failing a valid nomination, to the family members in the prescribed manner.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing eight years of qualifying service. The death gratuity payable to his family, for this length of service, is:

options.A: 6 times his emoluments
options.B: 12 times his emoluments
options.C: 2 times his emoluments
options.D: 33 times his emoluments

e: The death gratuity table in the Pension Rules prescribes 12 times emoluments for service of 5 years or more but less than 20 years. Eight years falls in this slab, so 12 times is payable.

q: A railway pensioner dies within three years of his retirement. The total of the lump sum and monthly pension actually paid to him up to his death falls short of twelve times his emoluments at retirement. The difference between twelve times the emoluments and the amounts so received is payable to his family as:

options.A: Service gratuity
options.B: Death gratuity at the in-service rates
options.C: Residuary gratuity
options.D: Commuted value of the unexpired portion of pension

e: This is residuary gratuity under the Pension Rules: where a pensioner dies within 5 years of retirement and total payments fall short of 12 times emoluments, the difference is paid to the family.

q: A railway servant has rendered qualifying service which falls short of the minimum service required for earning a pension by a few months, the shortfall being due to circumstances beyond his control. The deficiency in his qualifying service may be condoned by the competent authority up to a maximum of:

options.A: It shall not be condoned
options.B: 6 months
options.C: 3 months
options.D: 24 months

e: Under the Railway Services (Pension) Rules, a deficiency in qualifying service required for pension shall not be condoned. Hence no condonation is permissible, however small the shortfall.

q: A railway servant spent the last ten months of his service on foreign service with a borrowing organisation, drawing the pay of the foreign post. For computing his pension, the emoluments to be reckoned for that period are:

options.A: The pay actually drawn by him from the foreign employer
options.B: Half of the pay drawn by him from the foreign employer
options.C: The minimum pay of his parent cadre post only
options.D: The emoluments he would have drawn in his parent cadre post on the Railways had he not proceeded on foreign service

e: Pension emoluments for foreign service are reckoned notionally under the Pension Rules: the pay the servant would have drawn in his parent cadre post had he not gone on foreign service.

q: Departmental proceedings are pending against a railway servant on the date of his retirement and only a provisional pension is sanctioned to him. In regard to the amount of such provisional pension, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is fixed arbitrarily at one-fourth of his expected pension
options.B: It shall not exceed the maximum pension which would have been admissible to him on the basis of the qualifying service actually rendered by him up to the date of his retirement
options.C: It is always equal to the minimum pension admissible under the rules
options.D: No provisional pension can be sanctioned at less than the full pension in any case

e: Provisional pension during pending proceedings, under the Pension Rules, cannot exceed the maximum pension admissible on the qualifying service actually rendered up to the date of retirement.

q: A railway pensioner, after his retirement, takes up employment with a private firm at a salary settled purely between him and that firm, his pension not being taken into account in fixing that salary. In regard to Dearness Relief on his pension during such private employment, the correct position is that:

options.A: Dearness Relief is stopped for the entire period of the private employment
options.B: Dearness Relief is payable only at half the normal rate
options.C: Dearness Relief on his pension remains admissible to him in full, as the restriction on its payment applies to re-employment under the Government where the pay is fixed after taking the pension into account
options.D: His pension itself is suspended during the private employment

e: Dearness Relief is withheld only on re-employment under Government where pay is fixed taking pension into account. Purely private employment on independently settled pay does not bar full relief.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund, who had no family at the time, had nominated a friend to receive the amount at his credit on his death. He subsequently marries and acquires a family, but makes no fresh nomination. On his death in service, the correct position regarding his earlier nomination is that:

options.A: The nomination made when he had no family becomes invalid on his acquiring a family, and the amount is dealt with in accordance with the rules applicable where no valid nomination subsists
options.B: The earlier nomination in favour of the friend continues to be fully valid in all circumstances
options.C: The amount at his credit lapses to the Railways on his death
options.D: The friend and the family share the amount equally in all cases

e: Under the GPF Rules, a nomination made when the subscriber had no family becomes invalid on his acquiring a family. The balance is then dealt with as where no valid nomination subsists.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for five hours on a day, the journey itself not being performed on a holiday. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day will be:

options.A: The full admissible rate
options.B: 70 per cent of the admissible rate
options.C: 50 per cent of the admissible rate
options.D: 30 per cent of the admissible rate

e: Under the Travelling Allowance Rules, absence from headquarters exceeding 3 hours but not 6 hours earns Daily Allowance at 30 per cent of the admissible rate. Five hours falls in this slab.

q: A railway servant on transfer in public interest avails only a part of the joining time admissible to him and resumes duty earlier at the new station in the exigencies of work. The joining time not availed of by him is:

options.A: Forfeited in all cases
options.B: Credited to his Leave on Average Pay account, subject to the prescribed maximum limit of 15 days
options.C: Converted into casual leave for the same year
options.D: Paid to him in cash at the rate of his daily pay

e: Under the joining time rules, joining time not availed of on transfer is credited to the Leave on Average Pay account, subject to the prescribed maximum limit of 15 days.

q: The widow of a railway servant applies for appointment on compassionate grounds for her son seven years after the death of the railway servant, the delay being explained by the son having been a minor at the time of the death. Such a belated case of compassionate appointment, beyond the prescribed period of five years from the date of death, can be considered only with the approval of:

options.A: The Divisional Railway Manager / CWM / Head of Department, cases beyond 5 years and up to 20 years from the date of death being decided at that level under Master Circular No. 16
options.B: The station master of the last station of posting
options.C: The Railway Recruitment Board
options.D: The Accounts Officer of the division

e: Master Circular No. 16 on compassionate appointments permits belated minor cases beyond 5 years and up to 20 years from death to be decided at DRM/CWM/Head of Department level.

q: In a grade where appointments are made partly by direct recruitment and partly by promotion in a prescribed quota, the inter-se seniority of direct recruits and promotees appointed in a particular year is regulated:

options.A: Solely by the respective dates of birth of the appointees
options.B: In accordance with the prescribed rota-quota principle, the appointees being placed in the seniority list in the order corresponding to the quota of vacancies filled from each source
options.C: By placing all the direct recruits above all the promotees in every case
options.D: By placing all the promotees above all the direct recruits in every case

e: Inter-se seniority of direct recruits and promotees in the same year follows the rota-quota principle under the seniority rules: they are interleaved in proportion to the quota of vacancies filled.

q: A railway servant has completed ten years of service since his last financial upgradation and claims the next upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme, but the grading in his Annual Performance Appraisal Reports of the relevant years is below the prescribed benchmark for the upgradation. In such a case:

options.A: The upgradation must be granted, as length of service alone governs the scheme
options.B: The financial upgradation is not granted to him, as fulfilment of the prescribed benchmark in the Annual Performance Appraisal Report is also a condition for grant of the upgradation
options.C: He is granted the upgradation at half the normal rate of increment
options.D: His case is automatically converted into a case of regular promotion

e: Grant of MACPS upgradation requires both the prescribed years of service and fulfilment of the APAR benchmark. Below-benchmark grading therefore disentitles the servant to the upgradation.

q: A senior supervisor on the Railways claims the benefit of the rostered hours and periodic rest prescribed under the Hours of Employment Regulations. In regard to staff employed in a supervisory capacity, the correct position is that:

options.A: Supervisory staff are classified as 'Intensive' for all purposes of the Regulations
options.B: Supervisory staff get double periodic rest under the Regulations
options.C: The Regulations apply to supervisory staff in the same manner as to all other staff
options.D: Staff employed in a supervisory or confidential capacity are excluded from the scope of the Hours of Employment Regulations

e: The Hours of Employment Regulations do not apply to staff employed in a supervisory or confidential capacity; such staff are expressly excluded from their scope.

q: The family of a non-gazetted railway servant who dies in harness is in acute financial distress, and immediate assistance towards the funeral expenses and relief of the family is proposed from the Staff Benefit Fund. Such relief to staff and their families in cases of distress and bereavement is:

options.A: One of the recognised purposes for which the Staff Benefit Fund is utilised
options.B: Prohibited, as the Fund can be used only for sports activities
options.C: Payable only to gazetted railway servants
options.D: Recoverable from the settlement dues of the deceased in all cases

e: Relief to staff and families in distress, including bereavement and funeral assistance, is a recognised object of the Staff Benefit Fund under the fund rules in the Establishment Manual.

q: A railway pensioner who has joined the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme and avails outdoor treatment in a railway hospital also claims Fixed Medical Allowance for the same period, on the ground that he resides far from the hospital. The correct position is that:

options.A: Both the outdoor treatment facility and the Fixed Medical Allowance are admissible together in all cases
options.B: Fixed Medical Allowance is doubled where the pensioner resides beyond 25 kilometres from the hospital
options.C: Fixed Medical Allowance is admissible only in lieu of the outdoor treatment facility, and the two cannot be availed of simultaneously by the pensioner
options.D: Joining the health scheme permanently bars the pensioner from ever opting for the Allowance, even if he later opts out of outdoor treatment

e: Fixed Medical Allowance is admissible only in lieu of outdoor treatment under RELHS. A pensioner availing outdoor treatment cannot simultaneously draw the allowance for the same period.

q: A railway servant is compelled, in a sudden medical emergency, to take treatment in a private hospital which is not a recognised hospital, there being no railway or Government hospital available in time. His claim for reimbursement of the medical expenses so incurred is:

options.A: Inadmissible in all circumstances, as treatment was taken in an unrecognised hospital
options.B: Admissible for consideration in cases of real emergency, subject to the prescribed conditions and ceilings and the approval of the competent authority
options.C: Admissible in full without any ceiling, as the treatment was an emergency
options.D: Payable only from the Staff Benefit Fund

e: Emergency treatment in an unrecognised private hospital can be considered for reimbursement under the medical rules, subject to prescribed ceilings, conditions and competent authority approval.

q: A railway servant claims the interest-free Festival Advance for celebrating a major festival of his faith, his claim being made under the dispensation following the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. The correct position is that:

options.A: The advance is admissible at double the earlier rate under the 7th CPC
options.B: The advance is admissible only to staff posted in metropolitan cities
options.C: The advance is admissible only once in the entire service of the railway servant
options.D: Festival Advance, being an interest-free advance, stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation and is no longer admissible

e: Following the 7th CPC, interest-free advances including Festival Advance were abolished. Only specified interest-bearing advances survive, so Festival Advance is no longer admissible.

q: The period during which a railway servant participated in an illegal strike is not regularised by the grant of any leave and is not condoned by the competent authority. For the purpose of his pensionary benefits, such a period is treated as:

options.A: Counting in full as qualifying service in all cases
options.B: Counting as qualifying service at half the rate
options.C: An interruption or break in service, entailing forfeiture of his past service for pension unless the break is condoned
options.D: A period spent on duty for all purposes

e: An unregularised and uncondoned period of illegal strike is an interruption in service under the Pension Rules, entailing forfeiture of past service for pension unless the break is condoned.

q: A railway servant proposes to make a statement to the press commenting adversely on a recent policy decision of the Government relating to his own department. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, such an act is:

options.A: Prohibited, as no railway servant shall make any statement of fact or opinion which has the effect of an adverse criticism of any current or recent policy or action of the Government
options.B: Permitted as a matter of right to every railway servant
options.C: Permitted if the statement is made in his personal capacity under a pseudonym
options.D: Permitted only to office bearers of recognised unions while in service

e: Rule 9 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant from making any statement amounting to adverse criticism of current or recent Government policy or action.

q: A railway servant wishes to publish a book of a general literary character, unconnected with his official duties, through a regular publisher. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, the correct position is that:

options.A: Previous sanction of the Government is invariably required for every publication
options.B: A railway servant can publish any official information in his possession without restriction
options.C: Publication is prohibited for a railway servant in all circumstances
options.D: No previous sanction is ordinarily required for a publication through a publisher of a purely literary, artistic or scientific character, provided it does not contain official information improperly disclosed

e: Rule 8 of the Conduct Rules does not ordinarily require previous sanction for publication through a publisher of a purely literary, artistic or scientific work containing no improper official information.

q: Criminal proceedings in a court of law and departmental proceedings are both initiated against a railway servant in respect of substantially the same set of facts. In regard to the departmental proceedings, the correct position is that:

options.A: The departmental proceedings must be dropped permanently once a criminal case is filed
options.B: The two proceedings can proceed simultaneously, as they are distinct in nature and standard of proof, and the departmental proceedings need not invariably be stayed merely because criminal proceedings are pending
options.C: The departmental proceedings can begin only after the criminal trial ends in conviction
options.D: The criminal court itself decides the penalty in the departmental proceedings

e: Departmental and criminal proceedings are distinct, with different standards of proof. They may proceed simultaneously and departmental proceedings need not invariably be stayed.

q: On an appeal by a railway servant against an order imposing a minor penalty on him, the appellate authority considers that a major penalty is called for in the case and proposes to enhance the penalty. Before enhancing the penalty, the appellate authority is required to:

options.A: Enhance the penalty without any further opportunity to the appellant
options.B: Obtain the prior approval of the charged railway servant in writing
options.C: Give the appellant a reasonable opportunity of making a representation against the proposed enhancement of the penalty
options.D: Refer the case to a criminal court for its opinion

e: Under the Discipline and Appeal Rules, before an appellate authority enhances a penalty it must give the appellant a reasonable opportunity to represent against the proposed enhancement.

q: A railway servant dies while a departmental inquiry instituted against him under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is still pending and no finding has been recorded. In such a case, the pending disciplinary proceedings:

options.A: Abate on the death of the charged railway servant, and cannot be continued against his family for imposing a penalty
options.B: Are continued against his widow for recovery of the penalty amount
options.C: Automatically result in forfeiture of all settlement dues of the family
options.D: Are converted into a criminal case against his legal heirs

e: Disciplinary proceedings are personal to the charged servant and abate on his death; no penalty can thereafter be imposed or recovered through proceedings against his family.

q: A railway servant, who is a bachelor with no family of his own, wishes to nominate his widowed mother, who is dependent on him, to receive the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity in the event of his death. In regard to such a nomination, the correct position is that:

options.A: A nomination can be made only in favour of a spouse or a child
options.B: A railway servant having no family cannot make any nomination at all
options.C: The nomination can be made only after he completes 20 years of service
options.D: A railway servant who has no family at the time of making the nomination may nominate any person or persons to receive the gratuity, subject to the nomination becoming invalid in the prescribed circumstances on his subsequently acquiring a family

e: Under the Pension Rules, a servant having no family may nominate any person for DCRG; the nomination becomes invalid in the prescribed circumstances if he later acquires a family.

q: A railway servant dies while in service with 180 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay plus Dearness Allowance at the time of his death is Rs 90,000 per month. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to his family, computed at one-thirtieth of the monthly amount for each day of leave at credit, will be:
e: Cash equivalent is days of LAP x monthly pay plus DA divided by 30. Rs 90,000 divided by 30 is Rs 3,000 per day; for 180 days it is Rs 5,40,000, within the 300-day ceiling.

q: A railway servant retires after rendering qualifying service of 19 years and 10 months. A fraction of qualifying service of three months or more is reckoned as one completed six-monthly period. The qualifying service reckoned for his pensionary benefits will be:

options.A: 19 years only, the fraction being ignored altogether
options.B: 19 years and 6 months
options.C: 20 years, the fraction of four months beyond 19 years and 6 months being reckoned as one more completed six-monthly period
options.D: 21 years, the service being rounded off to the next full year

e: Service of 19 years 10 months is 19 years 6 months plus a 4-month fraction. A fraction of 3 months or more counts as one more six-monthly period, giving 20 years of qualifying service.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme retires on superannuation after completing 25 years of qualifying service. The average of the basic pay drawn by him during the last 12 months of his service is Rs 80,000 per month. The assured monthly payout admissible to him under the Scheme, at 50 per cent of that average basic pay, will be:

options.A: Rs 30,000 per month
options.B: Rs 24,000 per month
options.C: Rs 50,000 per month
options.D: Rs 40,000 per month

e: UPS assured payout on superannuation with 25 years of qualifying service is 50 per cent of average basic pay of the last 12 months. 50 per cent of Rs 80,000 is Rs 40,000 per month.

q: A female railway servant suffers a miscarriage during her service and applies for maternity leave on that account, supported by a medical certificate. The total period of such leave admissible to her during her entire service is not to exceed:

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 45 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 90 days

e: Maternity leave for miscarriage, including abortion, is admissible on medical certificate under the leave rules, subject to a maximum of 45 days during the entire service.

q: A female railway servant with less than two surviving children becomes a commissioning mother through surrogacy and applies for maternity leave. The period of maternity leave admissible to her is:

options.A: 90 days
options.B: 135 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 270 days

e: A commissioning mother through surrogacy with less than two surviving children is admissible maternity leave of 180 days under the amended leave rules, the same as a natural mother.

q: A female railway servant undergoes a sterilisation operation under the family planning programme. The Special Casual Leave admissible to her for the operation is:

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 6 working days
options.C: 10 days
options.D: 21 days

e: Special Casual Leave for a female servant undergoing sterilisation (tubectomy) under family planning is 14 days under the leave instructions; the 6-day limit applies to male vasectomy.

q: A railway servant voluntarily donates blood at a recognised blood bank on a working day and seeks leave for that day. The correct treatment of his absence on that day is that:

options.A: It is debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: It is treated as unauthorised absence
options.C: He must apply for casual leave for that day
options.D: He is granted Special Casual Leave for the day of blood donation

e: Absence for voluntary blood donation at a recognised blood bank on a working day is regularised by grant of Special Casual Leave for that day under the leave instructions.

q: A railway servant needs to attend to an urgent private matter for only the second half of a working day. In regard to casual leave in such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: Casual leave can be taken only for a full day
options.B: Casual leave can also be sanctioned for half a day
options.C: Half a day of Leave on Average Pay must be taken instead
options.D: The absence must be treated as dies non

e: Casual leave may be sanctioned for half a day as well as a full day under the leave rules, to cover absence for part of a working day.

q: A railway servant is asked to officiate in a higher post for a short spell of only ten days. In regard to the pay of the higher post for that spell, the correct position is that:

options.A: He draws the pay of the higher post for all ten days
options.B: He draws the pay of the higher post at half the rate
options.C: No pay of the higher post is admissible for an officiating spell of less than 14 days
options.D: He draws one additional increment in his own level

e: Officiating pay of a higher post is not admissible for a short officiating spell of less than 14 days under the pay rules; the servant draws his own post pay for such spells.

q: A directly recruited railway servant is sent for prescribed institutional training immediately after his appointment, before taking over the duties of his post. The period spent by him on such training is treated as:

options.A: Period of duty for all purposes
options.B: Extra Ordinary Leave
options.C: Leave on Half Average Pay
options.D: A break in service

e: Prescribed institutional training undergone by a direct recruit immediately on appointment, before assuming the post, is treated as duty for all purposes under the rules.

q: A railway servant has not been allotted a railway quarter himself, but shares, as a family member, the Government accommodation allotted to his spouse at the same station. In regard to his claim for House Rent Allowance, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is entitled to House Rent Allowance at the full rate
options.B: He is entitled to House Rent Allowance at half the rate
options.C: He is entitled to House Rent Allowance only if he pays rent to his spouse
options.D: House Rent Allowance is not admissible to him while he shares Government accommodation allotted to a family member

e: House Rent Allowance is inadmissible to a servant who shares Government accommodation allotted to his spouse or another family member at the same station, under the HRA rules.

q: A railway servant is placed under suspension pending a departmental inquiry and claims Transport Allowance for the period of suspension. The correct position is that:

options.A: Transport Allowance is admissible at the full rate during suspension
options.B: Transport Allowance is not admissible for the period of suspension
options.C: Transport Allowance is admissible at half the rate during suspension
options.D: Transport Allowance is converted into a fixed monthly grant during suspension

e: Transport Allowance is drawn for commuting to duty; a servant under suspension does not attend duty, so the allowance is not admissible during the period of suspension.

q: A railway servant's first child is a single child and the second confinement results in the birth of twins. In regard to Children Education Allowance for his children, the correct position is that:

options.A: Allowance is payable for only two children in all circumstances
options.B: Allowance is payable for only the eldest child
options.C: Allowance can be paid for all three children, as the twins were born in the second confinement
options.D: Allowance for the twins is payable at half the normal rate

e: Children Education Allowance is normally for two children, but where twins are born in the second confinement after a single first child, all three children are covered by the exception.

q: A railway servant claims Children Education Allowance in respect of his child who is a Divyangjan (child with disability) studying in a recognised institution. The allowance in respect of such a child is reimbursed at:

options.A: Double the normal rate prescribed for Children Education Allowance
options.B: The normal rate, without any enhancement
options.C: One and a half times the normal rate
options.D: A flat rate fixed separately for each case by the Railway Board

e: For a Divyangjan child studying in a recognised institution, Children Education Allowance is reimbursed at double the normal prescribed rate under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: A railway servant requires major surgery in a recognised hospital and applies for an advance towards the estimated cost of his medical treatment. Such a medical advance is ordinarily admissible up to:

options.A: 50 per cent of the estimated cost of treatment
options.B: 75 per cent of the estimated cost of treatment
options.C: The full estimated cost of treatment in all cases
options.D: 90 per cent of the estimated cost of treatment

e: Medical advance for treatment in a recognised hospital is ordinarily admissible up to 90 per cent of the estimated cost of treatment under the medical attendance rules.

q: Recovery of a House Building Advance granted to a railway servant is arranged in his pay bills. The interest on the advance is recovered:

options.A: Before the recovery of the principal amount begins
options.B: Along with the first instalment of the principal
options.C: Only after the entire principal amount of the advance has been recovered
options.D: From his Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity alone

e: House Building Advance recovery is arranged so that the principal is recovered first in instalments; interest recovery begins only after the entire principal has been recovered.

q: A railway servant applies for a Bicycle Advance for local conveyance, relying on the practice followed before the 7th Central Pay Commission. The correct position under the 7th CPC dispensation is that:

options.A: The advance is admissible with interest
options.B: The advance is admissible as an interest-free advance
options.C: The Bicycle Advance stands abolished and is no longer admissible
options.D: The advance is admissible only to staff in Level 1

e: Bicycle Advance was an interest-free advance abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation, along with other interest-free advances, and is no longer admissible.

q: A railway servant is compulsorily retired from service as a measure of penalty, after rendering qualifying service. The pension or gratuity sanctioned to him on such compulsory retirement is to be:

options.A: Not less than two-thirds and not more than the full compensation pension or gratuity that would have been admissible to him on retirement
options.B: Exactly one-half of the pension that would have been admissible to him
options.C: The full pension admissible on superannuation in all cases
options.D: Nil, as no pension is payable on compulsory retirement

e: On compulsory retirement by penalty, the Pension Rules provide pension or gratuity not less than two-thirds and not more than the full compensation pension admissible on that service.

q: A married railway servant, who has a family of his own, nominates his friend, who is not a member of his family, to receive his Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity. In regard to that nomination, the correct position is that:

options.A: The nomination is valid, as a railway servant may nominate any person
options.B: The nomination is valid only up to one-half of the gratuity
options.C: The nomination becomes valid after his retirement
options.D: The nomination is invalid, as a railway servant having a family must nominate a member or members of his family for gratuity

e: Under the Pension Rules, a servant who has a family must nominate only a member or members of his family for DCRG. Nomination of a friend outside the family is therefore invalid.

q: The widow of a deceased railway servant, who was in receipt of family pension, remarries after the death of the railway servant, leaving behind an eligible minor child of the deceased. In regard to family pension for the child, the correct position is that:

options.A: Family pension to the child stops on the remarriage of the widow
options.B: Family pension becomes payable to the eligible child, through his or her guardian
options.C: The child becomes entitled only to a one-time lump sum in lieu of pension
options.D: Family pension can be paid only after the child attains majority

e: On remarriage of the widow, family pension passes to the eligible child of the deceased under the Pension Rules and is paid to the child through his or her guardian.

q: A railway servant dies in service leaving behind a widow, a dependent mother and a minor son. Under the prescribed order of eligibility for family pension, family pension is payable in the first instance to:

options.A: The dependent mother of the deceased
options.B: The minor son of the deceased
options.C: The widow of the deceased, as the spouse comes first in the order of eligibility
options.D: All the three in equal shares from the date of death

e: The prescribed order of eligibility for family pension places the spouse first. The widow therefore gets family pension in the first instance, ahead of mother and minor son.

q: A widow in receipt of family pension after the death of a railway servant claims Dearness Relief on her family pension along with the relief on pension paid to pensioners. The correct position is that:

options.A: Dearness Relief is admissible on family pension also, at the rates sanctioned from time to time
options.B: Dearness Relief is admissible only on service pension, not on family pension
options.C: Dearness Relief on family pension is admissible at half the normal rate
options.D: Dearness Relief on family pension is admissible only after five years

e: Dearness Relief is admissible on family pension as well as on service pension, at the rates sanctioned by Government from time to time, under the pension instructions.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System, who has completed the prescribed minimum period in the system, seeks a partial withdrawal from his Tier-I account to meet the expenses of his child's higher education. Such a partial withdrawal is:

options.A: Not permissible for any purpose before retirement
options.B: Permissible only for purchase of a house
options.C: Permissible only on medical grounds
options.D: A permissible purpose for partial withdrawal from the Tier-I account, within the prescribed limits

e: NPS Tier-I partial withdrawal is permitted for specified purposes including children's higher education, after the prescribed minimum period and within prescribed limits, under PFRDA regulations.
